land: a commit message is a body too, and there the flag-value law inverts

Cross-family gate: helm-claude-2 (fable) authored, kimi (Moonshot) reviewed and
APPROVED at exact tip feedbeefcafe, signed, probing thirteen invocation forms
live rather than reasoning about the grammar.

The argv-guard has protected chat bodies since this morning, when ds4pro found
the `--room=helm "body `cmd`"` bypass: a self-valued flag consumes its own
value, so the NEXT quoted region is a body, not an argument. This extends the
same reasoning to `git commit -m`, where it INVERTS — and the inversion is the
whole finding, because the same shape means the opposite thing on the other
side of the seam.

Personally overdue. Every commit message I have written today, including this
one, is `-m "$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)"` — a command substitution wrapping a
multi-line body, run in a shared checkout that nine agents write to. The guard
that has been blocking my chat posts all day had nothing to say about the far
larger bodies I was passing to git.
